rule.name: Invoke-Expression with Variable Input
rule.rule_desc: The code invokes an interpreter, process, dynamic expression, or template-execution mechanism. Trace executable selection and evaluated content to their trust boundaries.
rule.vuln_desc: If an attacker controls interpreted syntax or the operation selected, code or commands may run with the application’s privileges, allowing data theft, state changes, or service disruption.
rule.developer: Replace externally influenced evaluation with fixed operations and data-only inputs. Use separate argument arrays for processes, allowlist permitted operations, and keep untrusted text out of executable templates or expressions.
rule.reviewer: Trace the origin of the string passed to Invoke-Expression and confirm no attacker-controlled path reaches it. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

rule.name: Start-Process or cmd.exe with Variable Arguments
rule.rule_desc: The code invokes a process or shell execution API. Trace the executable, arguments, shell use, and source of externally supplied values.
rule.vuln_desc: If attacker-controlled data changes command syntax or executable selection, an attacker may execute commands with application privileges, read or modify files, or disrupt service.
rule.developer: Use a fixed executable with a separate argument array and avoid a shell where possible. Validate arguments for the selected program and allowlist permitted operations.
rule.reviewer: Verify argument sources and confirm no user-supplied data reaches process invocations unescaped. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

rule.name: ConvertTo-SecureString with PlainText
rule.rule_desc: The script converts plaintext into SecureString. Determine whether the original value is embedded, logged, or accessible through process arguments.
rule.vuln_desc: The original plaintext may disclose an active credential to script readers or diagnostic recipients; conversion does not remove copies already exposed.
rule.developer: Obtain credentials from a restricted secret store or a secure input mechanism, keep plaintext out of scripts and logs, and rotate active values that were exposed.
rule.reviewer: Verify that the source string is not hardcoded or logged. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

rule.name: Bypass Execution Policy
rule.rule_desc: The script contains an attempt to bypass an execution-policy or anti-malware inspection mechanism. Determine actual effectiveness and deployment context.
rule.vuln_desc: If the bypass is effective, unauthorized or malicious script behavior may evade a configured inspection or execution restriction. A textual marker alone does not prove that protection was bypassed.
rule.developer: Remove unnecessary bypass behavior, retain applicable inspection controls, and enforce signing, application control, and least privilege independently of execution-policy settings.
rule.reviewer: Verify whether the bypass is used in authorized automation or represents a security control bypass. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

rule.developer: Remove unnecessary bypass behavior, retain applicable inspection controls, and enforce signing, application control, and least privilege independently of execution-policy settings.
rule.reviewer: Any occurrence of these patterns in production code should be treated as a high-severity indicator of compromise or intentional security bypass. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

rule.name: TLS Validation Disabled via Callback
rule.rule_desc: The checked source contains a transport-security exception, insecure endpoint, or certificate-validation configuration. Resolve the effective policy and the connections it governs.
rule.vuln_desc: An attacker on the network may read or alter affected traffic if sensitive data travels over cleartext or the connection accepts an untrusted server. Normal HTTPS endpoints and correctly implemented validation do not establish exposure.
rule.developer: Use HTTPS with normal certificate-chain and hostname verification. Remove permissive production callbacks and broad transport exceptions; restrict any justified exception to a documented, non-sensitive endpoint.
rule.reviewer: Confirm no production code accepts all TLS certificates unconditionally. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.
